item.title: Gary Trent Jr. investigation gets quick response from Taylor Jenkins
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Gary Trent Jr. investigation gets quick response from Taylor Jenkins appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NBA’s investigation into Kawhi Leonard and the LA Clippers over cap circumvention was not the only one of that nature that was ongoing. The league had also launched an investigation into the Milwaukee Bucks regarding Gary Trent Jr.‘s new contract in free agency, the results of which have not yet been made public as it’s still an active investigation. In the meantime, Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins was asked about the ongoing investigation into Gary Trent Jr.‘s contract prior to the team’s game against the Los Angeles Lakers, and he acknowledged that his hands were essentially tied as far as commenting on the matter , as per Cameron Ezeir of CBS 58. “I can’t comment on that,” Jenkins responded. “My focus is on day-to-day trying to help this team build winning habits and build our culture. So everything that I’ve been talking about in press conferences, that’s what I’m leaning into with this group. Our focus is right now, how we get better, learn from what happened last night against the Knicks, all the things we’ve been working on the last couple months and try to play our best basketball tonight against the Lakers.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The nine-year veteran guard has been used sparingly by the Bucks this season . He missed four games due to an illness, but hasn’t seen the floor much in the seven games that he has been available to this point. Trent has appeared in only three games at a little over six minutes per game. He’s averaging 3.7 points with splits of 44.4 percent shooting from the field, 42.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 61.1 percent shooting from the free-throw line. item.description: ‘They All Viewed It as a Sign’ — Tony Romo’s Appearance on ESPN After CBS Exit Fuels Intrigue Over His Next Career Move Tony Romo’s return to television had an audience beyond the fans watching Monday Night Football. People who work with on-air talent were watching, too, and they saw a broadcaster keeping himself in the game. According to Puck’s John Ourand, Romo’s appearance with Pat McAfee offered a clue about his ambitions after leaving CBS. The destination remains uncertain, but several industry observers came away believing he wants another chapter on television. Tony Romo’s McAfee Cameo Catches the Industry’s Attention Romo joined McAfee’s ESPN2 “Field Pass” alternate broadcast during the Buffalo Bills’ 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 9. A guest spot was enough to get sports-business executives discussing where he might land next. “Several sports business types who deal with on-air talent were intrigued by Romo’s decision to use McAfee’s alt-cast to make his first post-CBS public appearance,” Ourand wrote . “They all viewed it as a sign that Romo intends to maintain a career in television, either in the booth or in a studio.” That leaves quite a bit of room for his next move. Calling games would put him back in familiar territory. A studio role would offer a different setting for the same football knowledge, with more opportunities to debate and react alongside other personalities. item.title: Ravens find a new kicker after losing Jake Moody
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Ravens find a new kicker after losing Jake Moody appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It did not take long for the Baltimore Ravens to find a replacement for kicker Jake Moody after he was signed by the Atlanta Falcons to their 53-man roster. Moody was with the Ravens’ practice squad before getting poached by the Falcons. With an open spot, Baltimore eyed a veteran journeyman to fill it, as reported by NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. “The Ravens are signing former (Miami) Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson following a workout today, source says. Patterson will kick for Baltimore this Monday against the (Los Angeles) Chargers,” wrote Garafolo on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In 22 games for the Dolphins, Patterson converted 34-of-38 field goals for 141 points. The Ravens will be his seventh team in six seasons after also playing for the Detroit Lions, the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cleveland Browns, the New York Jets, and the Atlanta Falcons. He had two stints with the Lions and the Browns. He was also a practice player for the Minnesota Vikings, the New England Patriots, and the Washington Commanders. Patterson went undrafted in 2021 after a four-year career at Memphis. The Ravens’ signing of Patterson earned mixed reactions on X. “Working out a group of kickers and picking one is so Ravens,” said @SackGambles. “Should have kept Justin Tugger!” wrote @iHardMan302. “The crazy part about it is, every team he’s been on, he’s been solid,” added @TruVisionsz. “Now, let’s hope Baltimore doesn’t leave the game in the kicker’s hands. Please get it together!” pleaded @Charlie_A85. “The way that team is going, they should let me try out. I’m probably just as good,” commented @BKat99. The Ravens will try to end their four-game skid against the Chargers. item.title: Defense, a shot-stopper helped Wyoming advance to state final
item.description: SUNBURY, Ohio – Teddy Peterson rejoined the Wyoming High School soccer program this season after focusing on football for the past two years. The Wyoming junior goalkeeper, who has a lot of experience in net in club ball, made the biggest save of his career. He saved the final penalty kick by Bay Village Bay, giving the Cowboys a 6-5 win in the shootout after a 0-0 draw Nov. 11 in the Ohio High School Athletic Association Division IV boys soccer semifinals at Big Walnut High School. Wyoming (16-4-3) plays Worthington Christian in the state final 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, the home of the Columbus Crew. Wyoming was 2021 state champions and also made the semis in 2022. Bay finishes 17-2-5. It was a rematch of last year’s state semifinals, when Bay scored late in overtime to win it. “Last year we were at this field,” head coach Ryan Derge said. “They gave us a great fight. We gave them a great fight. We were two minutes away from going to PKs. This is very sweet for all of us, being able to come back and rectify in our minds what we lost." The teams played 110 minutes of scoreless soccer as both teams played intense defense. Wyoming’s best chances came from a couple of headers, which the Bay keeper saved from close range. Bay had a couple of shots from the side clip the crossbar and bounce away, a few inches from being a goal. “Both defenses were good tonight,” Derge said. “You feel it could be (0-0). I think both teams were just so well coached.” Brayden Strong, the senior anchor of the defense, was proud of his whole team. “We were just playing really good as a whole,” he said. “Our midfield was helping out. It was just an outstanding game by everyone today. And it showed at the end when we all got to celebrate with our amazing fans that came out. Just shows how strong our community is, it’s just an amazing feeling.” It went down to penalty kicks. The teams were tied 4-4 after five and then it became one for each team until there was a winner. Both teams made their sixth kick. Junior Liam Hagerman started the seventh round with a successful kick, then Peterson made the save the Cowboys needed. “He got two on his hands and he was able to get the third,” Derge said. “He's quite a shot-stopper. item.title: Trevor Megill Misses Out on NL Reliever of the Year Award 2026
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill (29) celebrates after winning Game 5 and World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 28, 2026. Mark Hoffman / Milwaukee Journal Sentinel / USA TODA… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Milwaukee Brewers are still basking in the glow of their first World Series title , but their star in the bullpen, Trevor Megill, has missed out on National League Reliever of the Year. The reliever was 30/33 in save opportunities in the regular season while posting a 0.89 WHIP, 2.63 ERA, and striking out 69 in 61 2/3 IP. The Brewers chose to rely heavily on their bullpen during their NLCS win and during the World Series, and Megill was central to that strategy. He matched his WHIP from the regular season in eight appearances while saving five games. Trevor Megill Loses NL Reliever of the Year Megill didn’t have a clear path to the majors for the first several years of his career, bouncing between the San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs and Minnesota Twins. He was eventually traded to the Brewers in 2023 for a player to be named later, in this case Taylor Floyd , who never reached Major League Baseball. It was in Milwaukee that Megill began to thrive, becoming their full-time closer during the 2024 season en route to being named to the 2025 All-Star team, his first accolade. Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill (29) throws a pitch against the Tampa Bay Rays during the ninth inning in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. item.title: Walker Kessler joins elite club in quick fashion
item.description: The Lakers’ Walker Kessler grabbed his 2,000th rebound against the Bucks on Wednesday, becoming the 11th-fastest player in NBA history to reach 2,000-plus points, 2,000-plus rebounds and 500-plus blocks. Kessler is the third-fastest active player to reach that line, trailing only Victor Wembanyama and Anthony Davis. Los Angeles Lakers’ Walker Kessler dunks during an NBA basketball game against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Milwaukee. AP Photo/Aaron Gash Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks for the Lakers, who entered Wednesday’s game with the league’s best record (10-2). Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) shoots against Atlanta Hawks forward Onyeka Okongwu (17) in an NBA basketball game, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Atlanta. AP Photo/Mike Stewart The Lakers acquired Kessler in July in a sign-and-trade from the Jazz for two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps on top of a four-year, $130 million deal. The 25-year-old Kessler only played five games last season after suffering a torn labrum in his left shoulder that required surgery. Kessler has made an immediate impact for the Lakers, who have won six games in a row . He entered Wednesday’s game leading the NBA in contested shots (140) and has been their defensive anchor , finishing with a double-double in six of his last seven contests. item.title: 7 free agents Chiefs should consider signing after NFL trade deadline
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs acquired star wide receiver Josh Downs in a last-minute deal with the Indianapolis Colts at the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but general manager Brett Veach's work is far from over. While the Chiefs can no longer trade for new players, the pool of veteran talent still available in free agency is astonishing. From All-Pro wide receivers to a Pro Bowl offensive lineman and a former NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, Kansas City's front office doesn't lack options if it wants to land one more big-name talent to shore up the Chiefs' depth chart for the second half of the 2026 regular season. Here are seven free agents Kansas City should take a look at in the coming days and weeks: WR Tyreek Hill Perhaps the most obvious choice, a reunion with Hill would be totally transformative for the Chiefs' offense — assuming the five-time All-Pro wideout is fully healthy and ready to play. OT Taylor Decker This 2024 Pro Bowler could help bring stability to the edges of Kansas City's offensive line and give Decker an opportunity to chase a ring while protecting Patrick Mahomes. DB Marshon Lattimore Kansas City is rumored to have pursued cornerbacks at the trade deadline, but the addition of Lattimore — the 2017 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year — would be a shot in the arm for Steve Spagnuolo's defense. WR Curtis Samuel Though he may have lost a step, Samuel could help Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes as a versatile runner-receiver with legitimate big-play ability. OL Jonah Williams Williams has plenty of experience blocking for an elite quarterback in Joe Burrow, but the Chiefs would have to do their due diligence on the shoulder injury that prematurely ended his 2025 campaign with the Arizona Cardinals . DB Jimmie Ward Though he hasn't played since 2024, Ward's veteran savvy could be just what Kansas City's secondary needs in the back half of the regular season. DL Joey Bosa A longtime Chiefs nemesis after a career spent with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills , the addition of Bosa would give Kansas City a tested pass-rusher with plenty of motivation to win a championship in what would be his eleventh NFL season. item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Bringing back NC State icon, NFL star Philip Rivers is a home-run hire for the football program and school. Philip Rivers is the only name that could help bring NC State football back into contention in the ACC. While the Wolfpack becoming an overnight contender for the College Football Playoff might be too much to ask, competing in the conference is not. Related: Miami With Best Path To College Football Playoff Title Game Rivers brings name value, and that is something you cannot ignore anymore. Not when it comes to money in college athletics and NIL swirling over the heads of everyone involved. Philip Rivers Set To Become The Next Head Football Coach At NC State According to multiple reports, a contract making Rivers the head football coach at NC State will be finalized on Friday. He asked to conclude his sixth season as head football coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama. Of course, we all remember when he briefly returned to the NFL after coaching high school athletes. Related: Iowa Deserves Position In Latest College Football Playoff Ranking Now, the 44-year-old is set to make the ultimate jump from the high school ranks to big-time college football. Success Followed Philip Rivers From The NFL To High School Football In Alabama Immediately, Rivers turned St. Michael Catholic into a contender in Alabama high school football. The Cardinals reached the state semifinals in both 2024 and again in 2025 under his guidance. Heading into this season, Rivers held a record of 44-16 overall, including a 25-9 mark while competing in Class 4A. Both years that St. Michael Catholic reached the final four, they lost to Jackson. This season, the Cardinals slipped to 6-5 overall, but went 5-2 in regional play, finishing third. They lost starting quarterback Gunner Rivers, Philip Rivers’ son, in the season opener. The younger Rivers would return after missing several games before returning in October. Top Talent Will Want To Play For NC State, Philip Rivers You better believe quarterbacks coming up through the high school ranks are going to want to play for Rivers. He knows everybody, has seen everything and has incredible connections to the NFL. High-end quarterback recruits will be flooding NC State under Rivers, and that will also bring top wide receivers, running backs, linemen and more to the program. item.title: Three Takeaways From the Flames' 3-1 Loss to the Rangers
item.description: The Calgary Flames came up short Wednesday night, falling 3-1 to the New York Rangers at the Scotiabank Saddledome. After a scoreless opening period, the Rangers needed just 59 seconds in the second to get on the board. Mika Zibanejad carried the puck into the Calgary zone, drove wide and fired a shot from a sharp angle that beat Cooley to give New York a 1-0 lead. Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Zibanejad struck again at 10:52, this time on the power play. After the Rangers moved the puck around the Calgary zone, Pavel Dorofeyev found Zibanejad at the top of the circle for a one-timer. The shot beat Cooley through the body and glove to make it 2-0. The Flames found an answer on the power play in the third period. At 7:41, Yegor Sharangovich sent the puck down low to Ryan Strome, who quickly spotted Adam Klapka in front of the net. Klapka jammed the puck past Joonas Korpisalo for his fourth goal of the season, cutting the deficit to 2-1. Calgary couldn’t find the equalizer, and Ty Kartye sealed the Rangers’ victory with an empty-net goal. Three Takeaways 1. Cooley’s strong home run comes to an end Cooley entered Wednesday’s game with an impressive 5-0-0 record in his previous five home starts, posting a 1.78 goals-against average and a .946 save percentage over that stretch. The Rangers handed him his first loss during that run, scoring twice in the second period to take control of the game. 2. Parekh continues to show his offensive potential Zayne Parekh provided one of Calgary’s more exciting moments in the opening period. The young defenceman carried the puck through the Rangers’ defence on an impressive individual rush, dangling his way toward the net before attempting to wrap around. Korpisalo got his blocker on the attempt to keep the game scoreless, but it was another glimpse of Parekh’s offensive creativity and ability to generate chances on his own. 3. Sharangovich continues to produce Sharangovich picked up an assist on Klapka’s third-period goal, extending a productive stretch for the Flames forward. He now has four points (one goal, three assists) over his last four games, providing some consistent offensive production for Calgary.

item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 10 of fantasy football has arrived, and with it come the usual calls of who to start and who to sit. Thursday Night Football kicks us off with the Washington Commanders against the New York Giants. Cam Skattebo is healthy again for the Giants, while Rachaad White had double-digit fantasy football performances in Weeks 6 and 8. Which running back should fantasy managers start in this class TNF matchup? RB Cam Skattebo, New York Giants In his second season in the NFL, Skattebo is averaging 10.1 fantasy points per week, putting him around RB28 status. With a matchup against the Commanders, who have allowed 694 rushing yards this season, and recent injuries to key defensive players, Skattebo looks favorable in Week 10. The Commanders held Skattebo in check in Week 5, allowing the Giants' running back only 59 yards on 13 carries. But with injuries to Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, the Commanders rush defense has slipped in recent weeks. The Commanders have allowed six rushing touchdowns this season, and Skattebo will be looking to add to his tally of two touchdowns on the season. Skattebo will be the main RB for the Giants, with Devin Singletary acting as his backup. RB Rachaad White, Washington Commanders Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White (1) rushes during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect White is averaging 10.0 fantasy points this season, but he has put up impressive fantasy point totals in Weeks 2, 6, and 8. Against the Giants, White only managed 3.0 fantasy points, but he was coming off of a shoulder injury that kept him out of Week 4. The Giants' defense has allowed 989 rushing yards this season, averaging about 123.6 yards per game for opposing running backs, making White look like a good choice for Week 10. White also has an upside as a pass-catcher, with the running back turning two receptions into 41 yards against the Rams in Week 9. White has been the main running back for Washington since Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on IR, with Austin Ekeler serving as his backup. Final Verdict While the Giants' defense has allowed more rushing yards this season, Skattebo should be the go-to fantasy pick in Thursday night's matchup. Skattebo carries a higher ceiling than White, and Skattebo will likely be the workhorse for the Giants' offense, especially if J.J. McCarthy feels any lingering effects of the hip injury sustained in Week 9. item.title: Son Heung-min says divisions at heart of South Korea team resolved
item.description: Son Heung-min has been called up by South Korea for friendlies next month against Saudi Arabia and Qatar (Philip FONG) Son Heung-min and four other South Korean players said Thursday they had put their differences aside after reports of bitter internal divisions at the heart of the national team. South Korean football has been mired in controversy since their hugely disappointing exit in the group stage of the World Cup, after which unpopular coach Hong Myung-bo quit. In the fallout, reports emerged in local media of a split involving the 34-year-old skipper Son and some of the other players, including Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae. Son and Kim, together with Lee Jae-sung, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan, issued a joint statement to fans apologising and saying it was time to move on after they held talks. "First of all we would like to sincerely apologise to the Korean public and football fans for the concern caused by recent reports concerning the national team," the statement said. "At our recent meeting we gathered to share our thoughts on the national team openly and honestly. "By listening directly to one another and discussing matters we had not had sufficient opportunities to address, we were able to gain a better understanding of each other's positions." During their talks they said they looked at what went wrong at the World Cup, admitting they were still hurting from the experience. "Our discussions began with the question of what needs to change to ensure that we do not repeat the same mistakes," they said in the statement. They added: "We now intend to put unnecessary controversy behind us and focus on building a stronger national team together." Spanish coach Robert Moreno took over from Hong on an interim basis, with his contract reportedly set to expire this month. South Korea play Saudi Arabia in Qatar on Friday before another friendly, against Qatar, four days later. The matches were originally designed as build-up to the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia but the tournament was last week postponed to December next year. bur-pst/dh

item.title: ‘LeBron (James) on LePoster,’ ‘Zero Gravity’ — Jayson Tatum’s Monster Dunk Over 76ers Star Sends NBA World Into Frenzy
item.description: Jayson Tatum’s dunk over LeBron James brings back 2018 memories and sparks reactions during his first matchup with Jaylen Brown. Jayson Tatum dunked on LeBron James during the Boston Celtics’ 123-101 rout of the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, bringing back memories of a moment from eight years earlier and sparking plenty of reaction online. The game also carried another storyline for the six-time All-Star, who was facing Jaylen Brown for the first time since his longtime Celtics teammate was traded to Philadelphia. NBA Community Reacts to Jayson Tatum’s LeBron James Poster and Jaylen Brown Moment The dunk came with 6:06 left in the third quarter, one possession after Tatum blocked VJ Edgecombe’s layup and grabbed the rebound. He then worked through a double team before throwing down a one-handed rim-rattling slam over James to push Boston’s lead to 73-67. “It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It’s been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it’s a basketball play,” the 28-year-old said after the game . By Wednesday morning, the Celtics had summed up the play in two words: “Zero gravity.” “Pardon My Take” had its own description : “Tatum puts LeBron on LePoster.” The dunk also immediately drew comparisons to Tatum’s rookie season, when he threw one down over the four-time NBA MVP in Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference finals. “Tatum turned back the clock on LeBron,” SportsCenter wrote . Barstool Sports Celtics analyst Dan Greenberg added : “Time is a flat circle.” The attention then shifted to Brown, whose first meeting with his former teammate had already drawn interest before tipoff. After the dunk, Brick Center reacted : “Tatum dunked on LeBron. The camera IMMEDIATELY cut to Jaylen Brown.” NBA/NFL insider Matt Wallace also highlighted their pregame interaction. “Jayson Tatum walked over before tip-off tonight to show love to his old teammate Jaylen Brown. Tapped his arm, tapped his chest, nothing but respect. Brown looked right through him. Wouldn’t even acknowledge him. Just kept spinning the ball like Tatum didn’t exist. Tatum took the high road and let it go,” Wallace noted . The 2024 NBA Finals MVP later said he had not been focused on the exchange. “I’m just focused on coming out and doing what’s best for my team. Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson. He played well tonight,” Brown said . Brown finished with 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting in 26 minutes, along with 4 turnovers and a game-worst minus-27. Asked about the same pregame moment, Tatum dismissed the idea that there was anything more to it. “Like I said, there are no headlines about anything like that. I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there, compete, have some fun, and try to get a win,” he said . Jacob Misiorowski is the National League’s Cy Young Award winner after the Milwaukee Brewers ace was finally announced as the 2026 winner on Wednesday. Coming off a sensational second season in the big leagues, Misiorowski got another reason to celebrate in the offseason. In addition to the World Series title he won with the Brewers by beating the Tampa Bay Rays in this year’s edition of the Fall Classic, the hard-throwing Misiorowski is now the fourth Brewer in franchise history to win the Cy Young. But there’s more . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Because Jacob Misiorowski won a World Series and a Cy Young Award in the same year, he also joined an extremely exclusive group of pitchers in MLB history. “The Miz has won the NL Cy Young. Jacob Misiorowski joins Randy Johnson and Justin Verlander as the only pitchers since 2000 to win both the Cy Young and the World Series in the same season,” SportsCenter shared via a social media post on X (formerly Twitter). Misiorowski put on a masterclass on nearly every night he pitched in 2026. Through 30 starts, he went 16-5. His ERA (1.80), total strikeouts (252) and WHIP (0.802) were all the best not just in the National League but in both leagues. Still just 24 years old, Misiorowski has so much in front of him, even though he’s already accomplished what countless others never achieved in their entire baseball careers. As long as he’s healthy, Misiorowski should be an intimidating pitcher to deal with opposing batters in years to come, including in 2027, when the Brewers look to defend their crown. item.title: Devin Booker and the Suns are committed to working together for the rest of his career
item.description: Devin Booker and the Suns are committed to working together for the rest of his career originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ever since the Phoenix Suns selected Devin Booker 13th overall in the 2015 NBA Draft, they have been committed to bringing winning basketball to the city. The results have been mixed, but it has been clear that Booker deserves to be the star. He has been the Suns ' best player over the past decade, cementing his place as one of the franchise's all-time greats. They were only two wins away from a championship in 2021, but the Milwaukee Bucks got away with the victory. Devin Booker is focused on staying as the Suns' star player In the 2026-27 NBA season, the Suns are still a middle-of-the-road team. However, Booker has remained productive for the Suns. He has lived up to his role as the team's superstar, averaging 25.1 points and 4.8 assists per game this season. Unfortunately, it seems that the Suns are far away from a championship. They want to win a title, but the Suns might n not have the contender-worthy roster that they had in the early 2020s when Booker had the likes of Mikal Bridges, Deandre Ayton, and Chris Paul with him. MORE: Devin Booker is firm in his chase for a championship with the Suns This has led to discourse regarding Booker potentially asking out and looking for a challenge elsewhere. Despite that, it seems that Booker and the Suns are together in their quest to win a title. "From every indication that I've got, the Phoenix Suns want to keep Devin Booker, and they want to continue to build around him. For Devin Booker, he wants to be a Sun for life, ideally... It's about trying to make the team better around him," Michael Scotto said about Booker's place on the team while on SiriusXM NBA Radio . It is definitely a tough situation for Booker and the Suns. However, they are committed to each other, as they want to keep competing and prove that they can be competitive against any team. This is a club that has spent 13 years hiring and firing the same structurally doomed manager – same shellshocked eyes, same irresolvable macro-problems – and the last eight years almost but not quite doing this to Pochettino. item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. The flamin’ pitch drop experiment began in 1930 and is designed to demonstrate how an apparent solid (pitch) behaves like an extremely viscous liquid. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. Without the need for intercontinental travel, perhaps other readers can now appreciate what it’s like to watch Arsenal win 1-0 ” – John Holtom. Continue reading...

After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
